# Re-entry Navigation Case Plan: Dillon Johnson

## 1. Executive Summary & Clinical Assessment
- **Participant Name:** Dillon Johnson
- **Location:** Charleston, SC
- **Risk Profile:** High Overall Risk
- **Primary Criminogenic Domains:** 1. Education/Employment | 2. Alcohol/Drug Problem | 3. Procriminal Attitude/Orientation
- **Current Stability Status:** At Risk (No driver's license, recent substance use history, high emotional volatility around workplace authority).

## 2. Core Behavioral Triggers & Facilitation Strategy (Turn90 Standards)
- **Triggers:** Perceived disrespect, feeling ignored, or administrative delays.
- **Escalation Pattern:** 'Cut Off' impulsive thinking leading to verbal outbursts, property destruction, and fleeing.
- **Facilitation Guidance:**
  - **Modeling Neutrality (Standard 1.5):** Staff must remain calm and neutral when Dillon expresses frustration or anti-social views. Reflect statements neutrally without debate.
  - **Managing Buy-In (Standard 3.2):** Explicitly link job retention and self-regulation to his primary goals: steady paychecks, independence, and staying off probation supervision.

## 3. Dynamic Targeted Action Items
1. **Workplace Stabilization & CBT Skill-Building:** Engage in daily CBT exercises focused on anger de-escalation, impulse control, and managing supervisor feedback.
2. **Substance Recovery Support:** Link with outpatient relapse counseling to address marijuana/edible triggers.
3. **Transportation Mapping:** Build dedicated transit routes using CARTA bus lines to ensure 100% on-time job attendance.

## 4. Supervision & Re-entry Accountability Roadmap
- **Weekly Goal:** Maintain full attendance in Turn90 programming and complete weekly check-ins with Probation Officer without breach.
- **30-Day Milestone:** Secure first-shift fair-chance employment along bus line; establish daily medication compliance for Hydroxyzine.
- **90-Day Milestone:** Maintain employment retention, demonstrate emotional de-escalation skills on site, and begin driver's license reinstatement plan.

# My Fresh Start Action & Resource Guide: Dillon Johnson

Welcome to your fresh start roadmap, Dillon! You have expressed a strong motivation to see life in a different light, overcome past obstacles, and build financial independence through steady work. This guide outlines your personalized resources, local job options, and weekly steps.

---

## 1. Key Community Resources & Referrals

### Transit & Getting to Work
- **CARTA (Charleston Area Regional Transportation Authority)**
  - **Services:** Fixed bus routes and workforce shuttles across Downtown, North Charleston, and West Ashley.
  - **Address:** Regional Stops throughout Charleston Tri-County
  - **Phone:** (843) 724-7420
  - **Link:** [Visit Website](https://ridecarta.com) | [Directions](https://maps.google.com/?q=Charleston+Area+Regional+Transportation+Authority)
  - **Action Step:** Work with your Navigator to obtain a monthly bus pass and map your route to employer sites.

### Healthcare & Prescription Maintenance
- **Welvista (Prescription Assistance)**
  - **Services:** Free maintenance prescription delivery for uninsured South Carolina residents (e.g., Hydroxyzine refill support).
  - **Phone:** (803) 933-9183
  - **Link:** [Visit Website](https://welvista.org)
  - **Action Step:** Submit an application with Navigator support to ensure uninterrupted access to maintenance meds.

- **Fetter Health Care Network**
  - **Services:** Sliding-scale primary medical, behavioral health, and dental care.
  - **Address:** 51 Nassau St, Charleston, SC 29403
  - **Phone:** (843) 722-4112
  - **Link:** [Visit Website](https://fetterhealthcare.org) | [Directions](https://maps.google.com/?q=51+Nassau+St,+Charleston,+SC+29403)
  - **Action Step:** Schedule a primary health checkup and routine prescription review.

### Recovery & Relapse Prevention
- **Charleston Center (DAODAS)**
  - **Services:** Intensive outpatient support, peer recovery support, and relapse prevention counseling.
  - **Address:** 5 Charleston Center Dr, Charleston, SC 29401
  - **Phone:** (843) 958-3300
  - **Link:** [Visit Website](https://charlestoncounty.org/departments/charleston-center/) | [Directions](https://maps.google.com/?q=5+Charleston+Center+Dr,+Charleston,+SC+29401)
  - **Action Step:** Connect with peer recovery specialists to build a solid relapse prevention plan for stress management.

### Driver's License Reinstatement
- **Center for Fathering / Father to Father Project**
  - **Services:** Driver's license restoration support, child support modification assistance, and legal barrier reduction.
  - **Address:** 4925 Lacross Rd, North Charleston, SC 29406
  - **Phone:** (843) 744-2126
  - **Link:** [Visit Website](https://scfathersandfamilies.com) | [Directions](https://maps.google.com/?q=4925+Lacross+Rd,+North+Charleston,+SC+29406)
  - **Action Step:** Meet with a case manager to check DMV record status and create a license recovery roadmap.

---

## 2. Top Fair-Chance Employer Matches

1. **Palmetto Logistics & Distribution Hub**
   - **Role:** Forklift Driver / Order Selector
   - **Pay:** $18.00 – $22.50 / hr
   - **Shift:** Day Shift (6:30 AM – 3:00 PM)
   - **Why It Fits:** Fair-Chance employer located along major transit corridors. Offers structured day shifts that align with your transit needs and physical stamina.
   - **Application Link:** [Apply Online / View Careers Page](https://www.indeed.com/jobs?q=warehouse+logistics&l=Charleston%2C+SC)

2. **Coastal Waste & Environmental Solutions**
   - **Role:** Transfer Station Associate / Route Helper
   - **Pay:** $18.50 – $22.00 / hr
   - **Shift:** Early Morning Day Shift (6:00 AM – 2:30 PM)
   - **Why It Fits:** Active second-chance partner that values reliability, teamwork, and strong work ethic. Great opportunity for reliable daily earnings.
   - **Application Link:** [Apply Online / View Careers Page](https://www.indeed.com/jobs?q=waste+route+driver+helper&l=North+Charleston%2C+SC)

3. **Brock Cabinets**
   - **Role:** Delivery Staff I (CHA)
   - **Pay:** $17.00 – $19.00 / hr
   - **Shift:** First Shift
   - **Why It Fits:** Located in North Charleston. Active team environment focused on warehouse assembly, staging, and material delivery.
   - **Application Link:** [Apply Online / View Careers Page](https://www.brockcabinets.com/)

---

## 3. Your 4-Week Milestone Checklist

- [ ] **Week 1: Transit & Medication Lock-In**
  - Finalize CARTA bus pass and test ride bus route to potential work sites.
  - Ensure prescription refills are confirmed with pharmacy / Welvista.

- [ ] **Week 2: Relapse Prevention & Employment Preparation**
  - Enroll in outpatient peer support / relapse coping group at Charleston Center.
  - Submit applications to 2 fair-chance employers with Navigator review.

- [ ] **Week 3: Interviewing & CBT Practice**
  - Practice workplace mock interviews with focus on de-escalating supervisor feedback.
  - Attend scheduled interviews and confirm work schedule.

- [ ] **Week 4: On-the-Job Success & Supervision Compliance**
  - Complete First Shift orientation and begin work.
  - Maintain 100% compliance with probation officer check-ins.

assessmentData.interviewTranscript:
CASE MANAGEMENT BRIEF
1. Risk Profile
Overall risk level: High
List top 3 criminogenic domains in risk order with top being number 1:
1. Education/Employment
2. Alcohol/Drug Problem
3. Procriminal Attitude/Orientation
Brief domain indicators:
Education/Employment: Currently unemployed with no months worked in the last year; history of losing
jobs due to attendance issues and workplace altercations.
Alcohol/Drug Problem: History of heavy daily marijuana and edible use that severely degraded mental
health, accompanied by poor financial management driven by drug habits.
Procriminal Attitude/Orientation: Recently arrested, indicating recent engagement in antisocial behavior;
expresses unfavorable attitudes toward convention during periods of distress.
2. Behavioral Indicators
Typical triggers: Feeling ignored, disrespected, or facing perceived slights (e.g., waiting at a counter without
eye contact).
Escalation tendencies: Rapidly escalates from frustration to yelling, verbal threats, property destruction
(throwing objects), and occasionally physical violence.
Decision-making patterns: Highly impulsive ("Cut Off" thinking); acts before thinking to immediately relieve
anger or avoid consequences (e.g., fleeing a scene to avoid jail).
Authority response style: Argumentative and historically combative with figures of authority (teachers,
supervisors).
Substance relapse patterns: Uses substances as a coping mechanism, leading to reckless spending and
worsening of anxiety/depression.
3. Pattern Over Time
Age at first justice involvement: 19
Number/frequency of incarcerations: At least 2 (one prison stint and recent 1-month jail term).
Recidivism timing patterns: Struggles significantly with sustained supervision; kept violating probation,
causing his sentence to be extended repeatedly.
Escalation or stability trends: Historical trend of aggressive outbursts and minor violence/property damage,
though he currently claims to want a life free of violence and anger.
Supervision violation history: High rate of probation breaches and absconding when confronted by law
enforcement.
4. Acute / Emergency Needs No acute needs identified at intake.
5. Stability Factors

-- 1 of 2 --

Housing stability level: Stable; currently residing in a structured transitional housing program that he finds
supportive.
Driver’s license status: None; relies exclusively on walking and public transit.
Education credential status: High School Diploma obtained.
Recent substance use: Early May 2026 (recent).
Employment history pattern: Sporadic; longest tenure is 2 years. Jobs typically end due to dissatisfaction
with pay, negative environments, and interpersonal conflict with management.
Supervision intensity: Active probation with Turn 90 condition.
6. Legal & Placement Constraints
Pending charges: None.
Court obligations: Standard probation terms and Turn 90 condition.
Supervision restrictions: Must maintain compliance to avoid further sentence extensions.
Sex Offender Registry requirement: No.
Movement/contact restrictions: None noted beyond standard probation requirements.
7. Responsivity & Engagement Profile
Literacy limitations: None noted.
Cognitive considerations: Diagnosed with anxiety and depression; currently taking medication (Hydroxyzine).
Trauma reactivity: Sensitive to feeling marginalized or ignored, which triggers acute anger and impulsivity.
Authority sensitivity: History of workplace and school altercations; staff should utilize de-escalation
techniques and maintain clear, respectful communication to avoid triggering defiance.
Motivation style: Intrinsically motivated to "see life in a different light" and address his mental health;
motivated by financial stability and utilizing his skills.
Learning preferences: Responds positively to supportive, structured environments, as evidenced by his
favorable view of his current transitional program.

-- 2 of 2 --
